handbookNote: Rhode Island Driver's Manual, April 2024 edition, Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles (dmv.ri.gov) -- fetched directly from the official PDF link on the DMV's own Operator Manuals page (dmv.ri.gov/licenses-permits-ids/permits-tests/operator-manuals, PDF at dmv.ri.gov/media/966/download) on 2026-08-17, converted to text, and saved in full to temp/handbooks/ri/driver.txt (this is a separate file from Rhode Island's existing notary handbook in that same folder, which was left untouched). Real exam mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the manual itself (Section I, 'Who must take the knowledge exam?'): the RI DMV computerized knowledge exam has a 90-minute maximum and consists of forty (40) multiple choice questions. The passing score/percentage is genuinely NOT published in the manual or on any RI DMV webpage checked (dmv.ri.gov Permits & Tests, Knowledge Exams, New License Permits, Operator Manuals pages were all fetched and reviewed) -- after thorough research this figure could not be confirmed from an official source, so it is left explicitly unconfirmed rather than guessed. The DMV's Knowledge Exams webpage does separately confirm that applicants who fail must wait at least 8 days before retaking the exam. This is an unusually rich, detailed 85-page manual covering GDL/licensing mechanics, distracted/drowsy/emotional driving, basic driving skills, signals and roadway markings (including roundabouts and a HAWK pedestrian signal), driving emergencies, motorcycles, defensive-driving systems (IPDE, the Smith System, zones, lane positions), sharing the road with trucks/pedestrians/bicyclists/school buses, a detailed DUI/DWI penalty schedule by age and BAC tier, collision procedures, law-enforcement stop procedures, required equipment, and a fine schedule -- comfortably supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question bank. Price matches this project's established Driver tier ($4.99), not a placeholder. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific, cited section of the fetched official manual text (a small number cite the DMV's own Knowledge Exams webpage for the 8-day retake wait); none are invented or generic 'common knowledge' items.
